definition: Offensive collateral estoppel is a type of collateral estoppel (also termed issue preclusion), the doctrine barring a party from re-litigating an issue decided against that party in an earlier action, even if the second action is significantly different from the first. Offensive collateral estoppel is asserted by a plaintiff in a suit to prevent the defendant from re-litigating an issue previously decided against the defendant. The opposite is defensive collateral estoppel, which is when the defendant asserts the estoppel.
